entradas.text: Back at the office, I was eagerly waiting for the decision of the Supreme Court regarding our change to the Constitution. I stood up from my chair and looked out the window.
Petr and Paskal were with me too. Petr was slouching on the couch on the right side of the office and staring at the ceiling. Paskal sat across from me. He was also eagerly waiting for the results.
The whole process had been tough on all of us. But now there was nothing left to do but wait for the Justices to cast their vote.
"What do you think Anton? Are we going to make history today?"
"I hope so."
"Yes. I'm sure of it."
"To be honest, I have a bad feeling about this."
entradas.menu: "To be honest, I have a bad feeling about this."

entradas.text: "So you trust Isabel to bring the votes?"
"Yes. I'm sure she will support the proposal."
entradas.menu: "Yes. I'm sure she will support the proposal."

entradas.text: "I don't know. But we have to hope for the best."
entradas.menu: "I don't know. But we have to hope for the best."

entradas.text: "No. I trust nobody."
Petr stared at the ceiling again.
"I hope so."
"Congratulations, sir. The constitutional changes are finalized with 8 Justices voting for the proposal."
"Congratulations, sir. The constitutional changes are finalized with 6 Justices voting for the proposal."
"Unfortunately, sir, the constitutional changes have been rejected with 6 Justices voting against the proposal."
"Unfortunately, sir, the constitutional changes have been rejected with 7 Justices voting against the proposal."
"Unfortunately, sir, the constitutional changes have been rejected with 8 Justices voting against the proposal."
"No. She told us that she will oppose us."
entradas.menu: "No. She told us that she will oppose us."

entradas.text: "That's not good."
"My real worry is Heron. I think we need his vote."
"I trust Isabel. According to Nia, she's a woman of her word."
Petr was with me, slouching on the couch on the right side of the office and staring at the ceiling.
"But I guess the important person in all this is Heron..."
"But anyway, we'll learn about the vote soon. The session is already underway."
"I hope Lucian managed to talk some sense into him."
"I doubt if anyone can."
"I hope so too. We'll see soon enough."
entradas.menu: "I hope so too. We'll see soon enough."

entradas.text: "I trust Lucian. I'm sure we have Heron."
entradas.menu: "I trust Lucian. I'm sure we have Heron."

entradas.text: "We'll see."
"Yeah... I guess you're right."
"But anyway, we'll learn about the vote soon. The session must have started already. What time is it?"
I looked at the tall case clock in the room. It was already twenty past eleven. The Court's voting session was scheduled to end in ten minutes.
"It's twenty past eleven."
"We have about ten minutes."
I did not reply.
"Anton?"
Petr slowly turned his head from where he was slouching to see the clock.
"Yeah. We have about ten minutes."
"Okay. We'll soon hear about the results then."
"Maybe you shouldn't have pushed the Court so much... Taking away their immunity was a bit too aggressive."
"By the way, what time is it?"
I looked at the tall case clock in the room. It was already twenty past eleven. The Court's voting session was scheduled to end in ten minutes.
I did not reply.
"Yeah. We have about ten minutes."
"We have about ten minutes."
"Anton?"
"It's twenty past eleven."
Petr looked at the clock.
"Okay. We'll soon hear about the results then."
He looked worried.
"I wouldn't blame them if they vote no."
"I had to do it, Petr."
"What's done is done. There's no point in going on about it."
entradas.menu: "What's done is done. There's no point in going on about it."

entradas.text: I did not reply.
"Petr. Shut up."
"Fine."
"You're right..."
"Did you, though?"
"Anyway..."
He yawned and stretched out on the couch.
"But anyway..."
He rose from his slouch and stretched.
"I don't know if you noticed, but Kesaro has been getting popular in the Assembly recently."
"Our party's been supporting him on a lot of bills, some of which have already reached you."
"What do you make of this? I think he's a very dangerous man, Anton. We can't let him divide our party."
"I agree. We have to watch him closely."
entradas.menu: "I agree. We have to watch him closely."

entradas.text: "I have no problem with bipartisan bills passing the Assembly."
entradas.menu: "I have no problem with bipartisan bills passing the Assembly."

entradas.text: "I don't make anything out of it. It's expected that he'd get the support of our conservative wing."
entradas.menu: "I don't make anything out of it. It's expected that he'd get the support of our conservative wing."

entradas.text: "His party only holds 40 seats, Anton. Yet he manages to pass bills..."
"Maybe we shouldn't allow our party to be so generous with what they support..."
"I don't make anything out of it. It's expected that he'd get the support of our conservative wing."
entradas.menu: "I don't make anything out of it. It's expected that he'd get the support of our conservative wing."

entradas.text: "I have no problem with bipartisan bills passing the Assembly."
entradas.menu: "I have no problem with bipartisan bills passing the Assembly."

entradas.text: "I don't know if you noticed, but Kesaro has been very popular in the Assembly as of late.
"Our party's been supporting him on a lot of bills, some of which have already reached you."
"I agree. We have to watch him closely."
entradas.menu: "I agree. We have to watch him closely."

entradas.text: "What do you make of this? I think he's a very dangerous man, Anton. We can't let him divide our party."
"Maybe we shouldn't allow our party to be so generous with what they support..."
"His party only holds 40 seats, Anton. Yet he manages to pass bills..."
"That man is trouble."
"Mr. Kibener aside, we seem to be in a very troubling situation regardless."
"I don't want to be so negative right as we're waiting for the results but..."
"The political violence on the streets is not stopping. I am not sure if this was the right time for reform..."
"With the decrease in our law enforcement budget, I am feeling very stressed about the future of our country, Mr. President. Mrs. Morgna and Mrs. Graf seem to be under a lot of stress."
"And we've got enough trouble aside from him."
"The violence on the streets hasn't stopped since we came in. I am not sure if this is the right time for reform anymore, Anton..."
"I don't want to be so negative while we're waiting for the results, but..."
"With the decrease in our law enforcement budget, I'm not sure if this is ever going to stop."
Suddenly, Livia entered the room. In her hands was a large object wrapped in straw paper.
"Good day to you, Mr. President. Am I interrupting anything?"
"It's okay, Livia. What happened?"
"Yes, you are. What is it?"
"No. Please come in. Is there a problem?"
entradas.menu: "No. Please come in. Is there a problem?"

entradas.text: "Good day to you, Mr. President and Mr. Beniwoll. Am I interrupting you?"
Suddenly, Livia entered the room. In her hands was a large object wrapped in straw paper.
"It's okay, Livia. What happened?"
"Yes, you are. What is it?"
"No. Please come in. Is there a problem?"
entradas.menu: "No. Please come in. Is there a problem?"

entradas.text: "The Chief Justice has sent you this."
She showed me the wrapped object.
"Thank you, Livia. You can leave it on my table."
entradas.menu: "Thank you, Livia. You can leave it on my table."

entradas.text: "Really? From Orso Hawker? Bring it here."
entradas.menu: "Really? From Orso Hawker? Bring it here."

entradas.text: "What is it?"
"I don't know... A painting maybe?"
"I'll just bring it to you."
She walked up to the table and gave it to me. I immediately started to remove the wrapping to reveal a framed photograph.
"Yes, sir."

It was an old black and white photograph of Tarquin Soll posing on a destroyed tank in Holsord Square. The building behind him had thousands of bullet holes on it and the clearly readable slogan 'Victory is close' written on its walls.
The date, 14 March 1929, was written in the corner with a black marker.
"He's obviously trying to send you a message, but--"
"Hi, Livia."
Noticing Petr on the couch, Livia reddened slightly. She gave a small wave, which Petr returned.
As soon as she left the room, Petr came up next to me and took a look at the photograph.
"Nice present."
"Yeah. A picture of Tarquin Soll. What a nice present..."
entradas.menu: "Yeah. A picture of Tarquin Soll. What a nice present..."

entradas.text: "Damn Orso..."
"This must be some kind of a message."
entradas.menu: "This must be some kind of a message."

entradas.text: "What do you think?"
"What is it?"
"Victory will be close, huh? Orso's getting ahead of himself."
Suddenly, Lucian rushed into the room.
"Mr. President! The vote has been concluded."
We immediately gathered around him.
"Yes! Congratulations, everybody."
"YES!"
Petr jumped up and down like a little kid.
"What!? No..."
Petr put his hands on his forehead.
"Damn Old Guard..."
"Congratulations, Anton!"
"Damn Old Guard..."
"We failed."
"This is a historic moment, Anton! We have changed Soll's Constitution of 1929... I am without words."
"This is just the beginning."
"We are writing history."
"We did it together."
"What do we do now?"
"It's not the end of the world."
entradas.menu: "It's not the end of the world."

entradas.text: "We're screwed..."
"Yeah... I guess."
"Big time."
"That stupid photograph from Orso too! They are mocking us..."
"I'll talk to the cabinet and arrange a meeting immediately. We have to plan our next steps."
"This failure will not reflect well with the public or the Assembly..."
"I am more scared of the Court. I'm a target for them now."
entradas.menu: "I am more scared of the Court. I'm a target for them now."

entradas.text: "We will get through it. This was just a failed proposal."
entradas.menu: "We will get through it. This was just a failed proposal."

entradas.text: "Arrange the meeting immediately."
"True. Mr. Hawker is the most dangerous of them all."
"I really want to believe in that..."
"Right away, sir!"
"Hell yeah, we did!"
"Damn right, we are!"
"Hell yes, it is!"
Petr approached to give me a hug.
We hugged each other.
I reached out my hand. He paused for a moment, looking slightly disappointed, before shaking it vigorously.
"You did well, Anton."
"Congratulations, sir. Today is a big day."
All of us immediately got to work to plan our next steps after our Supreme Court failure.
"You must also start preparing a speech to announce the changes, sir."
"I'll go ahead and reach out to the cabinet. We can celebrate this together over a meeting."
All of us immediately got to work to plan our next steps after our Supreme Court victory.
"Unfortunately, sir, the constitutional changes have been rejected. Only two of the Justices voted for our proposal."
"Unfortunately, sir, the constitutional changes have been rejected. Only one of the Justices voted for our proposal."
"Congratulations, sir. The constitutional changes are finalized with 7 Justices voting for the proposal."
"What do you think this means, Livia?"
entradas.menu: "What do you think this means, Livia?"

entradas.text: "Did Orso say anything to you about this?"
entradas.menu: "Did Orso say anything to you about this?"

entradas.text: "Thanks, Livia. You may go now."
I turned to Livia.
"No, but he's obviously trying to send you a message. I--"
Livia turned to leave.
"Mr. Vice President. I'll be leaving now."
"Especially after we decided to include the expansion of rights for the Bludish people."
